pick.headline: De Klerk unbans the ANC
pick.summary: On February 2, 1990, South African President F. W. de Klerk lifted the ban on the African National Congress and other organizations and announced that Nelson Mandela would be released.
pick.significance: The speech began the dismantling of apartheid and the negotiations that led to majority rule in 1994.
pick.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of February 5, 1990, carried a Moscow TASS text of a Soviet Foreign Ministry statement welcoming de Klerk's decision to free Mandela and lift the ban on the ANC and Communist Party as "a step in the right direction", while urging an end to the state of emergency.

alternates.headline: Syrian forces besiege Hama
alternates.summary: On February 2, 1982, an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood in the Syrian city of Hama began, and Hafiz al-Asad's forces crushed it over the following weeks, killing thousands.
alternates.significance: The Hama massacre ended the Islamist challenge to Asad for a generation. Damascus media largely kept silent about it.
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of February 4, 1982, carried Beirut's Voice of Lebanon reporting that Hamah had been encircled and under shelling and explosions since midnight, with dead seen on roads into the city and unrest spreading to Aleppo; the reasons were "not yet clear".
